results.note: The test asserts that the catalog-v2 request comes first (request #1). It then checks that the history start_time equals the later of the per-metric min_times (FlowOut 2020-02-01), and that both min_times are recorded in source_field. A companion test at line 156 shows _history_rows raises before any history request when start_time is earlier than min_time.

A mocked empty response for a start_time equal to the catalog min_time returns (), meaning genuinely no rows. The out-of-window case (line 156) raises ValueError and makes no history request, so the two cases are handled differently. The out-of-window test calls the private _history_rows directly, because the public recipe always starts at min_time.

There are 12 requests: 1 catalog and 11 paginated history pages, run on a fake clock. For every group of 10 consecutive requests, the test asserts they span at least 6s. The limiter (ingest/fetchers/coinmetrics.py:41) spaces calls 0.7s apart, so 10 requests span 9×0.7 = 6.3s. No 429/throttle-retry path is tested.

The test asserts that the second request URL exactly equals the vendor-supplied next_page_url. Pagination stops when next_page_url is absent. The values come back as [1.0, 2.0] with matching timestamps, so no rows were dropped or duplicated. The loop in _history_rows sets params=None after the first page, so the URL is left unmodified.

The only live test is marked @pytest.mark.integration, and pyproject.toml:33 (addopts '-m not integration') deselects it from every gate. No evidence file for US-905 records a live run. The test also calls backfill_coinmetrics_asset_metrics directly rather than the public run_backfill entry point with persistence, so it would not count as an integration test even if it ran.
The US-905-C6 gate `uv run pytest -q` exited 0.

note: The offline tests (C1–C4) contain real assertions over MockTransport and are not faked. C5 is not met: the one live test is deselected by the default marker filter, there is no record of it ever running, and it bypasses the run_backfill entry point.
